gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Thunderbolt 5's storage gain is a PCIe-tunnel step (Intel: 'double the PCI Express data throughput', built on PCIe Gen 4) that only an M4 Pro/Max port exposes, that OWC's own ladder puts the same 80G enclosure at 'over 6000MB/s' on TB5 but 'up to 3800MB/s' on a TB4 port like the base M4's, that Howard Oakley found full TB5 speed needs macOS 15.3 or later, and that OWC limits PCIe Gen 5 SSDs inside to about 11 W average.
standout_why: Compared against the three cited pages: DPReview (M4 Pro MacBook Pro test; says TB5 was 1.2-1.8x USB4 'not quite realizing the theoretical 2x' and gives no cause), OWC's how-to-choose blog (only 'your drive's speed is capped by your computer's port', no figures per port) and the ACASIS product pages (could not be opened: HTTP 429 on every attempt, so their content is unverified). None explains why ~6,000 MB/s is the ceiling, none gives the TB4-host fallback number from the maker, none mentions the macOS 15.3 requirement, and none gives the Gen 5 SSD power limit. Uncited rank-4 picklog.cc does state the 64 Gbps PCIe Gen4 x4 wall (via Sabrent and ChargerLAB), so the wall itself is only partly new; the Apple-port mapping, the OWC per-host ladder, the 15.3 note and the 11 W limit are new.
decides: Confirms the pick is conditional on the chip, and sharpens it: a TB5 enclosure on a base M4 MacBook Pro (Apple: 'Thunderbolt 4 (up to 40Gb/s)') is a TB4 device, OWC's own figure 'up to 3800MB/s', so the shopper should buy a 40 Gbps USB4 enclosure instead. On M4 Pro/Max (Apple: 'Thunderbolt 5 (up to 120Gb/s)') the enclosure reaches 'over 6000MB/s', and Oakley's measured ceiling is about 6 GB/s, so a PCIe 4.0 SSD (990 Pro class) is the right pairing; a PCIe 5.0 SSD adds no bandwidth and OWC warns it must average 11 W or less in the bus-powered 1M2 80G. The shopper must also run macOS 15.3 or later for full TB5 speed. Any TB5 enclosure on an M4 MacBook Pro keeps TRIM and SMART (Oakley: NVMe interface trims; SMART works over Thunderbolt/USB4, not USB 3.x), so that does not separate the candidates.

findings.label: Intel: what Thunderbolt 5 changes for storage
findings.value: 80 Gbps bi-directional; up to 120 Gbps Bandwidth Boost for displays; 'Double the PCI Express data throughput for faster storage and external graphics'; built on 'PCI Express Gen 4' and 'USB4 V2'
findings.note: Intel gives no Gbps figure for PCIe on this page. Arithmetic: a PCIe Gen 4 x4 link is 4 lanes × 16 GT/s × 128/130 ≈ 63 Gbps ≈ 7.9 GB/s raw each way; a Gen 3 x4 link (Thunderbolt 4) is half, ≈ 3.9 GB/s. That is why TB5 enclosures top out near 6-7 GB/s and TB4 near 3-3.8 GB/s, well below the 80 or 40 Gbps link number.

findings.label: Howard Oakley: macOS version needed for full Thunderbolt 5 speed
findings.value: 'macOS 15.3 or later is required for full TB5 performance'
findings.source_title: macOS Sequoia 15.3 has improved Thunderbolt 5 performance – The Eclectic Light Company (2025-02-04)
findings.note: Mac mini M4 Pro. Through a TB5 dock, USB4 SSD write rose from 2.3 to 3.8 GB/s and TB3 SSD write from 0.42 to 1.6 GB/s on updating 15.2 to 15.3. Single TB5 SSD was 'around 150%' of a USB4 SSD and '180-250%' of a TB3 SSD.

findings.label: Howard Oakley: measured TB5 vs USB4 SSD and the ceiling
findings.value: 5.2 / 5.5 GB/s read / write on Mac mini M4 Pro over TB5; 3.1 / 3.1 GB/s over USB4 on MacBook Pro M3 Pro; 'the maximum transfer rate it can achieve over its 80 Gb/s works out at 6 GB/s'
findings.source_title: Thunderbolt 5 SSDs are promising, but fill their cache quicker – The Eclectic Light Company (2025-01-30)
findings.note: Oakley calls a maker's 6.7 GB/s claim 'bogus'. Same TB5 SSD dropped from about 5.5 to 1.4 GB/s write after roughly 50 GB (SLC cache), so sustained write depends on the SSD chosen, not the enclosure. SSD model not named; macOS version not stated.

findings.label: Howard Oakley: TRIM and SMART over Thunderbolt/USB4 vs USB 3.x on macOS
findings.value: 'APFS and HFS+ will only Trim SSDs with an NVMe interface'; 'macOS can only access SMART indicators over FireWire, Thunderbolt and USB4 connections, and not over USB 3.x or earlier'
findings.source_title: Which external drives have Trim and SMART support? – The Eclectic Light Company (2024-04-09)
findings.note: OWC Express 1M2 on Apple silicon over USB4: full TRIM and SMART; same enclosure on an Intel Mac in USB 3.x fallback: TRIM but no SMART. Every M4 MacBook Pro port is TB4 or TB5, so any TB5 NVMe enclosure keeps both; this does not separate the candidates.

findings.label: DPReview test on M4 Pro MacBook Pro (cited rival)
findings.value: TB5 drive (OWC Envoy Ultra) 'around 1.2 to 1.8 times faster' than USB4 drive in synthetic tests, 'not quite realizing the theoretical 2x'
findings.source_title: Do photographers need the fastest external SSD? We tested three to find out | DPReview (2026-01-17)
findings.note: No MB/s figures and no mechanism given; the PCIe Gen 4 x4 tunnel and SLC cache explain the sub-2x result.
